answer: Sybil resistance can come from pricing admission on prior work: a new identity joins only after its hash sits in a public proof-of-labor pool, like a lotus grown from seeds anyone can inspect. Each node then mirrors the pool to verify, and a false claim sticks out like a crack in a mirror. Cloned identities share provenance, so the network treats them as one oasis plot, diluting their rewards until fake agents earn nothing.
